newsitem.title: USA: Value Health says new deal due to stock drop.
newsitem.headline: Value Health says new deal due to stock drop.

text.p: Value Health Inc said a recent decline in the stock of Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp prompted the revision of merger terms between the two companies.

"I think the uncertainty of what's happening in the stock is a reason. We wanted to take as much uncertainty out of the deal for our shareholders as was possible," said Value Health spokeswoman Judith Hyfield-Starr.

Value Health earlier announced the two companies agreed to revise terms of the deal to call for cash payment for Value Health shares. The original agreement called for Value Health shareholders to receive stock.

Shares of Columbia/HCA have fallen sharply in recent weeks following news of a federal probe into its El Paso, Texas facilities. The company has said it is cooperating with federal agents and has not been informed of allegations.

The original pact, which was valued at $1.3 billion when announced in January, did not set a collar or other mechanism to protect Value Health shareholders in case of a stock decline, Hyfield-Starr said.
